'''Oscar Randal-Williams''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} is a British mathematician and professor at the [[University of Cambridge]],<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~or257/ |title = Oscar Randal-Williams}}</ref> working in [[topology]].

== Career ==
Randal-Williams studied mathematics at the [[University of Oxford]] (MMath 2006, DPhil 2009), where he wrote his doctoral thesis ''Stable moduli spaces of manifolds'' under the supervision of [[Ulrike Tillmann]].<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=144052}}</ref> Since 2012 he has been at the [[University of Cambridge]], since 2017 as [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]], since 2020 as professor,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~or257/Short%20CV.pdf|title=Short CV: Oscar Randal-Williams|access-date=2024-04-11}}</ref> and since 2024 as the [[Sadleirian Professor of Pure Mathematics]].<ref>Cambridge University Reporter, Vol. CLIV:6, No 6716, 1 November 2023, p. 95</ref>

In joint work with [[Søren Galatius]], he studied moduli spaces of [[manifold]]s, leading to a sequence of papers about which his coauthor talked at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] 2014.<ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211209/eW-T4Diqn_8 Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20160306195642/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW-T4Diqn_8 Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite AV media| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eW-T4Diqn_8| title = ICM2014 VideoSeries IL6.4 : Soren Galatius on Aug15Fri | website=YouTube}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
In 2017 Randal-Williams received<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/30062017-1833/lms-prizes-2017 | title=LMS Prizes 2017 &#124; London Mathematical Society }}</ref> a [[Whitehead Prize]] from the [[London Mathematical Society]] and a [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/philip-leverhulme-prizes-2017 | title=Philip Leverhulme Prizes 2017 &#124; the Leverhulme Trust}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.maths.cam.ac.uk/features/oscar-randal-williams-understanding-moduli-spaces |title = Oscar Randal-Williams – understanding moduli spaces &#124; Features: Faculty Insights}}</ref> In 2018 he was awarded an ERC Starting Grant,<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results/biomechtools?search_api_views_fulltext=HToMS | title=Erc Funded Projects | access-date=1 August 2019 | archive-date=1 August 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801154326/https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results/biomechtools%3Fsearch_api_views_fulltext%3DHToMS | url-status=dead }}</ref> and in 2019 the [[Dannie Heineman Prize (Göttingen)|Dannie Heineman Prize]] of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] and the [[Oberwolfach Prize]]. In 2022 he was awarded the [[Clay Research Award]] jointly with Søren Galatius,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.claymath.org/events/news/2022-clay-research-award|title=2022 Clay Research Award &#124; Clay Mathematics Institute|website=www.claymath.org}}</ref> and spoke at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l6zVroyC7rM Oscar Randal-Williams: Diffeomorphisms of discs]</ref> In 2024 he was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Oscar Randal-Williams FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/oscar-randal-williams-36795/ |access-date=2024-05-20 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>
